pr_title: Ensure `RID`, `Callable`, and `Signal` are stored as strings
pr_body:
Prevents parser errors in `.tscn` and `.tres` files where the assignment would otherwise be empty.

Using just `RID()` instead of storing the value, might do so only for the empty `RID`, it is required for default values to work in `GDExtension` as `RID`s cannot be created from integers just like in `GDScript`, but since we weren't serializing them at all anyway I went for a simple solution. This also fixes that serializing an array containing any of these types is broken with `var_to_str`, currently `var_to_str([Callable(), Signal(), RID()])`, results in `[, , ]`, now it will instead give `[Callable(), Signal(), RID()]`, though it does so regardless of the value, not attempting to serialize, but `var_to_str` doesn't handle references anyway as it is.

This also fixes hints in the editor, where before hints for these types for functions with defaults would not print anything.

We should probably not serialize these types on default in `GDScript` exports, but I don't know how to approach that so just fixing the immediate issue here to start with.

* Fixes: #78380 (Fixes the immediate issue)
* Fixes: #64442

pr_comments:
Considering specifying this behavior on `var_to_str` like so:
```
[b]Note:[/b] This will return [code]RID()[/code], [code]Signal()[/code], and [code]Callable()[/code] for those types, regardless of the value, not storing any details about the actual value.
```

Added a fix to loading `RID` so it is typed as an `RID`, and also added support for storing them directly, storing `RID()` as such to ensure compatibility with `GDExtension`, also added documentation for the behavior, either of the second two commits are up for debate and will squash which ever are picked
Will squash if there's a consensus on the additional changes for storing `RID`s
Will look at unit tests but at the moment I am lacking the energy most likely, will take a look at doing so in the next few days but can do so in a separate PR as well

issue_context.title: Parse error when attempting to export var of Callable type in a resource
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.1.beta.a83eb16fb

### System information

Arch Linux

### Issue description

When attempting to have a scene load a resource that uses a script that exports a var of Callable type, a parse error will occur due to Callable not being serializable.

### Steps to reproduce

Create new project.
create a resource script that exports a Callable type:

```
class_name BreakStuff
extends Resource
@export var something: Callable
```

create a .tres file that uses the script.

create a scene that uses that resource, such as with a script like

```
extends Node
@export var stuff: Resource
```

set that resource to that .tres file.

close project and reopen.

Be greeted with error message about a parse error and be unable to open that scene.

Within plain text of .tscn file you can see a line that reads
something =

which causes a parse error as something has nothing to be set to.



### Minimal reproduction project

N/A
comments:
Happens from 4.0 to v4.0.3.stable.official [5222a99f5] aswell.

Probably is related to FormatResourceSaved not knowing how to handle Callable types, resulting in a serialization with an empty value? The script server allowing the user exporting Callables (and there's a `TYPE_CALLABLE` for property types so I don't think this is not allowed)?

![image](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/assets/7025991/1dba159c-c84a-48c4-89fe-3b838cec5dda)

Curiously, this is not the case for PackedScenes: exporting a `Callable` in a node with a value will not serialize the variable, even if it has a value, with or without `@tool`.
```gdscript
@tool
extends Node

@export var foo:Callable = bar

func bar() -> void:
	pass
```

Should be handled more graciously, but yes it isn't, and shouldn't be, possible to serialise callable

Should be documented if not already, and perhaps some warning in the script if exported, exports are by default marked with the storage flag
Got a PR open for solving the direct error, doesn't allow serializing `Callable`s, but that isn't supported in the binary format either so this brings parity to it

review_comments: To catch if future types are added, currently all types are present as far as I can tell
